claim: A transposon element was integrated into exon 3 of the Pclo genomic sequence, leading to a premature stop in the reading frame.
source: As shown in Figure 1A, the transposon element was integrated into exon 3 of the Pclo genomic sequence, leading to a premature stop in the reading frame.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the schematic of transposon insertion.

claim: Western blot analysis from postnatal day 2 (P2) rat brains confirmed the loss of Piccolo full-length protein.
source: Western blot analysis from postnatal day 2 (P2) rat brains as well as from primary hippocampal neuron lysates confirmed the loss of Piccolo full-length protein (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Bands at 560 kD as well as between 70–450 kD were detected in lysates from Pclowt/wt and Pclowt/gt brains, reflecting the expression of multiple Piccolo isoforms from the Pclo gene.
source: Bands at 560 kD as well as between 70–450 kD were detected in lysates from Pclowt/wt and Pclowt/gt brains (Figure 1C), reflecting the expression of multiple Piccolo isoforms from the Pclo gene (Fenster and Garner, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1C and cited literature.

claim: In brain lysates from Pclogt/gt animals, the dominant bands at 560 and 450 kD were absent, indicating the loss of the predominant Piccolo isoforms.
source: In brain lysates from Pclogt/gt animals, the dominant bands at 560 and 450 kD were absent, indicating the loss of the predominant Piccolo isoforms, though a few weaker bands at 300, 90 and 70 kD are still present (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Piccolo intensity at synapses (positive for VGlut1) was reduced by more than 70% in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Consistently, Piccolo intensity at synapses (positive for VGlut1) was reduced by more than 70% in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 1E), confirming the loss of most Piccolo isoforms from synapses.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunocytochemical data shown in Figure 1E with quantification showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.03, n = 586 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 0.35 ± 0.01, n = 718 synapses.

claim: Piccolo immuno-reactivity was absent in hippocampal brain sections from Pclogt/gt animals.
source: Similarly, Piccolo immuno-reactivity was absent in hippocampal brain sections (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistological staining shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Piccolo deficiency was associated with a slight decrease in the expression of Bassoon and the SV protein Synaptophysin.
source: Intriguingly, Piccolo deficiency was associated with a slight decrease in the expression of Bassoon and the SV protein Synaptophysin (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The levels of the early endosome marker EEA1 were decreased by half in Pclowt/gt and Pclogt/gt lysates.
source: The levels of the early endosome marker EEA1 were most severely affected, its levels were decreased by half in Pclowt/gt and Pclogt/gt lysates (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1G showing EEA1: Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.03, Pclowt/gt = 0.44 ± 0.01, Pclogt/gt = 0.50 ± 0.02.

claim: The levels of the small Rab GTPase Rab5 were slightly increased in Pclogt/gt brain lysates.
source: In contrast, the levels of the small Rab GTPase Rab5 were slightly increased in Pclogt/gt brain lysates, whereas the levels of Dynamin were increased in both Pclowt/gt and Pclogt/gt brain lysates (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1G showing Rab5: Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.09, Pclowt/gt = 1.04 ± 0.11, Pclogt/gt = 1.22 ± 0.04.

claim: The number of Synapsin puncta per unit length of primary dendrite was not significantly different between Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: the number of Synapsin puncta per unit length of primary dendrite was not significantly different between Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunocytochemical data in Figure 1I showing Pclowt/wt = 0.27 ± 0.02, n = 27 primary dendrites; Pclogt/gt = 0.29 ± 0.02, n = 22 primary dendrites.

claim: The levels of several SV proteins were decreased in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Even though the number of synapses was not changed, the levels of several SV proteins were decreased in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 A, B, C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunocytochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The levels of the cytosolic SV-associated protein Synapsin were not affected by the loss of Piccolo.
source: A conclusion further supported by the fact that the levels of the cytosolic SV-associated protein Synapsin were not affected by the loss of Piccolo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 A and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunocytochemical data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing Synapsin: Pclowt/wt = 1.00 ± 0.01, n = 2773 puncta; Pclogt/gt = 0.99 ± 0.01, n = 1848 puncta.

claim: EM micrographs from Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons revealed the presence of synaptic junctions, with prominent postsynaptic densities (PSDs) formed onto axonal varicosities of Pclogt/gt neurons, with similar dimensions (length) to Pclowt/wt synapses.
source: EM micrographs from Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons revealed the presence of synaptic junctions, with prominent postsynaptic densities (PSDs) formed onto axonal varicosities of Pclogt/gt neurons, with similar dimensions (length) to Pclowt/wt synapses (Figure 2A,B,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2A, B, and E.

claim: The number of SVs/bouton was significantly reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: At many Pclogt/gt synapses, SVs (<50 nm diameter) were detected (Figure 2B), however the number of SVs/bouton was significantly reduced (Figure 2A,B,C), which is in line with the earlier observed reduced levels of Synaptophysin, Synaptotagmin and VGlut1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 2C showing Pclowt/wt = 51.73 ± 4.05, n = 52 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 38.08 ± 3.19, n = 59 synapses.

claim: The number of docked SVs at AZs was not altered in Pclogt/gt synaptic terminals.
source: Even though the total number of SVs was changed, the number of docked SVs at AZs was not altered in Pclogt/gt synaptic terminals (Figure 2D,H,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 2D showing Pclowt/wt = 1.49 ± 0.18, n = 59 AZs; Pclogt/gt = 1.67 ± 0.18, n = 40 AZs.

claim: Lower SV density in Pclogt/gt boutons was accompanied by a high number of endosome-like structures with diameters larger than 60 nm.
source: Intriguingly, lower SV density in Pclogt/gt boutons was accompanied by a high number of endosome-like structures with diameters larger than 60 nm (Figure 2A,B,F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 2F showing Pclowt/wt = 1.42 ± 0.24, n = 52 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 2.39 ± 0.38, n = 57 synapses.

claim: A slight, but non-significant, reduction in the amplitudes of excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSC) was observed in Pclogt/gt compared to Pclowt/wt neurons.
source: We performed whole cell patch clamp recordings from autaptic hippocampal neurons and observed a slight, but non-significant, reduction in the amplitudes of excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSC) in Pclogt/gt compared to Pclowt/wt neurons (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 3A showing Pclowt/wt = 1.0 ± 0.15, Pclogt/gt = 0.73 ± 0.10.

claim: The readily releasable pool of vesicles (RRP), determined by the application of hypertonic sucrose (5 s, 500 mM), was not altered in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Also the readily releasable pool of vesicles (RRP), determined by the application of hypertonic sucrose (5 s, 500 mM), was not altered in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 3D showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.15, Pclogt/gt = 0.83 ± 0.11.

claim: SV release probability (Pvr) and paired pulse ratio (PPR) (25 ms pulse interval) were not changed in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Similarly, SV release probability (Pvr) and paired pulse ratio (PPR) (25 ms pulse interval) were not changed in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 3B and C.

claim: The steady state EPSC amplitude at the end of a 10 Hz/5 s train stimulation was reduced in Pclogt/gt autapses.
source: However, the steady state EPSC amplitude at the end of a 10 Hz/5 s train stimulation was reduced in Pclogt/gt autapses, indicating impaired maintenance of synaptic transmission during intense vesicle fusion (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 3E showing Pclowt/wt : 34 cells, Pclogt/gt : 35 cells.

claim: Pclogt/gt neurons displayed a 30% reduction in FM4-64 intensity, consistent with a smaller TRP of SVs.
source: Next, we performed FM-dye uptake experiments (Smith and Betz, 1996) to determine the size of the total recycling pool (TRP) of SVs. Here, Pclogt/gt neurons displayed a 30% reduction in FM4-64 intensity, consistent with a smaller TRP of SVs (Figure 3H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM-dye uptake data in Figure 3I showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.01, n = 1026 puncta; Pclogt/gt = 0.69 ± 0.01, n = 867 puncta.

claim: FM1-43 dye was released at a much slower rate from Pclogt/gt than Pclowt/wt boutons.
source: Remarkably, FM1-43 dye was released at a much slower rate from Pclogt/gt than Pclowt/wt boutons (Figure 3J,K).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM1-43 unloading data in Figure 3K showing Pclowt/wt = 74.62 ± 0.6607, n = 244 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 45.47 ± 1.468, n = 155 synapses.

claim: The total amount of FM1-43 dye released after 90 s stimulation was significantly reduced in neurons lacking Piccolo.
source: Moreover, the total amount of FM1-43 dye released after 90 s stimulation was significantly reduced in neurons lacking Piccolo (Figure 3K).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM1-43 unloading data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: An increase in the number of GFP-Rab5 positive puncta along axons was observed in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Interestingly, we observed an increase in the number of GFP-Rab5 positive puncta along axons (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4C showing Pclowt/wt = 0.06 ± 0.004, n = 139 axon sections; Pclogt/gt = 0.08 ± 0.004, n = 143 axon sections.

claim: The number of GFP-Rab7 puncta along axons was reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Surprisingly, the number of GFP-Rab7 puncta along axons was reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 4B and C), indicating that the maturation of membranes within the endosome compartment from Rab5 positive early endosomes towards late Rab7 positive endosomes is affected by the loss of Piccolo (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4C showing Pclowt/wt = 0.11 ± 0.004, n = 139 axon sections; Pclogt/gt = 0.06 ± 0.004, n = 142 axon sections.

claim: The number of EEA1 immuno-positive puncta along axons was reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Indeed, the number of EEA1 immuno-positive puncta along axons was reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 4B and C), further indicating that the loss of Piccolo alters early endocytic membrane trafficking.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4C showing Pclowt/wt = 0.12 ± 0.01, n = 29 axon sections; Pclogt/gt = 0.09 ± 0.004, n = 34 axon sections.

claim: Rab5 levels were not altered at Synaptophysin positive boutons in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Quantifying intensities at Synaptophysin positive boutons revealed that while Rab5 levels were not altered (Figure 4D and G), EEA1 levels were decreased at Pclogt/gt synapses (Figure 4, E and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4G showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.03, n = 808 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 1.04 ± 0.05, n = 773 synapses.

claim: EEA1 levels were decreased at Pclogt/gt synapses.
source: Quantifying intensities at Synaptophysin positive boutons revealed that while Rab5 levels were not altered (Figure 4D and G), EEA1 levels were decreased at Pclogt/gt synapses (Figure 4, E and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4H showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.02, n = 4323 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 0.79 ± 0.02, n = 3939 synapses.

claim: The synaptic levels of mChRab7 are reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: The same is true for the synaptic levels of mChRab7; they are also reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 4F and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4I showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.03, n = 386 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 0.72 ± 0.02, n = 525 synapses.

claim: No differences in the levels of Rab5 and EEA1 were detected in the cell soma of Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Consistent with this concept, no differences in the levels of Rab5 and EEA1 were detected in the cell soma of Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The levels of somatic Rabex5 were significantly reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: However, the levels of somatic Rabex5 were significantly reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.07, n = 16 soma; Pclogt/gt = 0.65 ± 0.06, n = 15 soma.

claim: The intensities of dendritic Rab5 and EEA1 puncta are increased in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Intriguingly, along dendrites the intensities of Rabex5 puncta are not altered upon the loss of Piccolo (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 E and H), although the intensities of dendritic Rab5 and EEA1 puncta are increased in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: The numbers of GFP-2x-FYVE puncta per axon length were not different between Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: The numbers per axon length were not different between Pclowt/wt and Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C), suggesting that PI3P-positive organelles form normally.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C showing Pclowt/wt = 0.88 ± 0.05, n = 39 axons; Pclogt/gt = 0.80 ± 0.05.

claim: Pclogt/gt boutons had smaller GFP-2x-FYVE organelles than Pclowt/wt boutons.
source: Using structure illumination microscopy (SIM), we observed that on average Pclogt/gt boutons (Bassoon and Synaptophysin positive) had smaller GFP-2x-FYVE organelles than Pclowt/wt boutons (Figure 4—figure supplement 2G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by super-resolution imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2G and H.

claim: The levels of Rab5 at PI3P-positive organelles are decreased in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: In Pclogt/gt axons, the amount of endogenous EEA1 as well as Rab5 at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta was significantly decreased (Figure 5B,C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 5C showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.02, n = 1645 puncta; Pclogt/gt = 0.81 ± 0.02, n = 1233 puncta.

claim: The amount of EEA1 at PI3P-positive organelles is reduced in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: In Pclogt/gt axons, the amount of endogenous EEA1 as well as Rab5 at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta was significantly decreased (Figure 5B,C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 5D showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.04, n = 1634 puncta; Pclogt/gt = 0.37 ± 0.02, n = 1169 puncta.

claim: The fraction of early endosomes (GFP-2x-FYVE/Rab5/EEA1) was reduced by about 70% in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: In contrast, the fraction of early endosomes (GFP-2x-FYVE/Rab5/EEA1) was reduced by about 70% (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 5F showing Pclogt/gt = 0.28 ± 0.10.

claim: Levels of Rabex5 at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta were decreased in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: In fact levels of Rabex5 at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta were decreased in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.04, n = 728 puncta; Pclogt/gt = 0.80 ± 0.03, n = 652 puncta.

claim: The fraction of GFP-2x-FYVE/Rabex5 double positive puncta is significantly increased in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Notably, the fraction of GFP-2x-FYVE/Rabex5 double positive puncta is significantly increased in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E showing Pclogt/gt = 1.49 ± 0.33.

claim: Those that are triple positive for GFP-2x-FYVE, Rabex5 and Rab5 are reduced by 40% in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: In contrast, those that are triple positive for GFP-2x-FYVE, Rabex5 and Rab5 are reduced by 40% (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F showing Pclogt/gt = 0.57 ± 0.14.

claim: Synaptophysin levels in neurons expressing Rab5S34N were decreased, which was similar in magnitude to that observed in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Interestingly, Synaptophysin levels in neurons expressing Rab5S34N were decreased (Figure 6A and C), which was similar in magnitude to that observed in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 6C showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.02, n = 204 synapses; Pclowt/wt + mCh-Rab5S34N = 0.75 ± 0.03, n = 139 synapses.

claim: The presence of Rab5S34N in Pclowt/wt neurons led to lower levels of EEA1 at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta as well as a smaller fraction of GFP-2x-FYVE/Rab5/EEA1 triple positive early endosomes.
source: Furthermore the presence of Rab5S34N in Pclowt/wt neurons led to lower levels of EEA1 at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta as well as a smaller fraction of GFP-2x-FYVE/Rab5/EEA1 triple positive early endosomes (Figure 6B,E,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 6E and G.

claim: The FM1-43 uptake efficiency during 60 mM KCl stimulation was reduced by about 20% in neurons expressing Rab5S34N.
source: In addition, we observed that the FM1-43 uptake efficiency during 60 mM KCl stimulation was reduced by about 20% in neurons expressing Rab5S34N (Figure 6H and I), representing a smaller TRP of vesicles.
evidence: The claim is supported by FM-dye uptake data in Figure 6I showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.01, n = 732 puncta; Pclowt/wt + mCh-Rab5S34N = 0.84 ± 0.01, n = 866 puncta.

claim: The expression of Rab5Q79L in Pclogt/gt neurons rescued endogenous Rab5 as well as EEA1 levels at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta.
source: Analyzing Rab5 and EEA1 levels at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta revealed a significant rescue of endogenous Rab5 as well as EEA1 levels in Pclogt/gt neurons (Figure 7A,B,C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 7C and D showing rescue of Rab5 and EEA1 levels.

claim: The expression of Rab5Q79L in Pclowt/wt neurons decreased EEA1 levels at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta.
source: Remarkably, the expression of Rab5Q79L in Pclowt/wt neurons had the opposite effect, decreasing EEA1 levels (Figure 7A and D), though total Rab5 levels were only slightly altered (Figure 7A and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 7D showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.04, n = 1066 puncta; Pclowt/wt (mCh-Rab5Q79L)=0.77 ± 0.04, n = 979 puncta.

claim: Synaptophysin levels increased upon the presence of dominant active Rab5Q79L in Pclogt/gt neurons.
source: Synaptophysin levels increased upon the presence of dominant active Rab5Q79L (Figure 7E and F), indicating that the loss of SVs in Pclogt/gt boutons is linked to altered Rab5 activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 7F showing rescue of Synaptophysin levels.

claim: In Pclogt/gt synapses harboring Rab5Q79L the amount of FM1-43 dye after 60 mM KCl stimulation was comparable or even higher than in Pclowt/wt neurons.
source: Here, we found that in Pclogt/gt synapses harboring Rab5Q79L the amount of FM1-43 dye after 60 mM KCl stimulation was comparable or even higher than in Pclowt/wt neurons (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM-dye uptake data in Figure 8B.

claim: Rab5Q79L expression in Pclogt/gt neurons did not restore FM1-43 unloading kinetics.
source: Surprisingly, Rab5Q79L expression in Pclogt/gt neurons did not restore FM1-43 unloading kinetics (Figure 8C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM-dye unloading data in Figure 8D showing Pclogt/gt = 47.24 ± 0.68, n = 361 synapses; Pclogt/gt(Rab5Q79L)=48.33 ± 0.53, n = 479 synapses.

claim: In Pclowt/wt neurons, the block of synaptic activity causes the levels of EEA1 to drop.
source: Interestingly, in Pclowt/wt neurons, the block of synaptic activity causes the levels of EEA1 to drop (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by TTX treatment data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1F showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.03, n = 1653 synapse; Pclowt/wt (TTX) = 0.72 ± 0.03, n = 1887 synapses.

claim: Silencing synapses in Pclogt/gt neurons had no effect on EEA1 levels.
source: However, silencing synapses in Pclogt/gt neurons had no effect on EEA1 levels, and only minor effects on the levels of Rabex5, Rab5 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B, C, E, F, H, I).
evidence: The claim is supported by TTX treatment data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The addition of Latrunculin significantly enhanced the levels of Rab5, but not EEA1 at GFP-2x-FYVE puncta.
source: We found that the addition of Latrunculin significantly enhanced the levels of Rab5, but not EEA1 (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by drug treatment data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Jasplakinolide was not able to enhance Rab5 and or EEA1 levels at GFP-2x-FYVE punta in boutons lacking Piccolo.
source: Consistently, Jasplakinolide was not able to enhance Rab5 and or EEA1 levels at GFP-2x-FYVE punta in boutons lacking Piccolo (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B), indicating that Piccolo`s role in F-actin assembly is not important for the formation of early endosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by drug treatment data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Pra1 localized to presynaptic terminals, co-localizing with Synaptophysin in Pclowt/wt neurons.
source: We found that Pra1 localized to presynaptic terminals, co-localizing with Synaptophysin in Pclowt/wt neurons (Figure 9A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunocytochemical data in Figure 9A and B.

claim: In Pclogt/gt neurons synaptic Pra1 levels were reduced.
source: However, in Pclogt/gt neurons synaptic Pra1 levels were reduced (Figure 9A,B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunocytochemical data in Figure 9C showing Pclowt/wt = 1 ± 0.03, n = 474 synapses; Pclogt/gt = 0.55 ± 0.02, n = 723.

claim: More than 80% of Pclo-Znf1-mCh puncta co-localized with Synaptophysin in Pclowt/wt neurons.
source: First, we observed that more than 80% of Pclo-Znf1-mCh puncta co-localized with Synaptophysin in Pclowt/wt neurons (Figure 9—figure supplement 1), demonstrating it is mainly localized synaptically.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 9—figure supplement 1 showing 83.82 ± 9.475% co-localization.

claim: The expression of Pclo-Znf1-mCh rescued Synaptophysin levels to greater than wildtype levels in both Pclogt/gt and Pclowt/wt boutons.
source: Second, the expression of Pclo-Znf1-mCh rescued Synaptophysin levels to greater than wildtype levels in both Pclogt/gt and Pclowt/wt boutons (Figure 10A and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 10D showing rescue of Synaptophysin levels.

claim: Pclo-Znf1-mCh over-expression restored Pra1 levels at Pclogt/gt synapses to even higher levels than in Pclowt/wt neurons.
source: Third, Pclo-Znf1-mCh over-expression also restored Pra1 levels at Pclogt/gt synapses to even higher levels than in Pclowt/wt neurons (Figure 10B and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 10E showing rescue of Pra1 levels.

claim: Synaptic EEA1 levels in Pclogt/gt neurons were significantly increased in the presence Pclo-Znf1-mCh.
source: Also synaptic EEA1 levels in Pclogt/gt neurons were significantly increased in the presence Pclo-Znf1-mCh (Figure 10C and F), further indicating that Pclo-Znf1-mCh supports the accumulation of synaptic Pra1 and along with it EEA1.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 10F showing rescue of EEA1 levels.

claim: Pclo-Znf1-mCh expression in Pclo neurons increased the ability of synapses to take up FM1-43 dye during 60 mM KCl stimulation.
source: Intriguingly, Pclo-Znf1-mCh expression in Pclo neurons also increased the ability of synapses to take up FM1-43 dye during 60 mM KCl stimulation. In Pclowt/wt as well as Pclogt/gt neurons, FM 1–43 levels were increased in the presence of Pclo-Znf1-mCh (Figure 11A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM-dye uptake data in Figure 11B.

claim: In Pclogt/gt neurons, Pclo-Znf1-mCh lead to a faster FM1-43 unloading rate compared to Pclogt/gt neurons, although the speed seen in Pclowt/wt neurons was not fully reached.
source: In contrast, in Pclogt/gt neurons, Pclo-Znf1-mCh lead to a faster FM1-43 unloading rate compared to Pclogt/gt neurons, although the speed seen in Pclowt/wt neurons was not fully reached (Figure 11C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM-dye unloading data in Figure 11D showing partial rescue of unloading kinetics.

claim: Piccolo plays a critical role in the activity dependent recycling of SVs.
source: Our study has shown that Piccolo plays a critical role in the activity dependent recycling of SVs.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the Discussion section, synthesizing the experimental findings.

claim: Piccolo loss of function reduces SV numbers as well as the recycling of SVs, without affecting the activity dependent docking and fusion of SVs.
source: Specifically, we find that Piccolo loss of function reduces SV numbers as well as the recycling of SVs, without affecting the activity dependent docking and fusion of SVs.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the Discussion section, synthesizing multiple experimental findings.

claim: Boutons lacking Piccolo accumulate endocytic vesicles that fail to mature into early endosomes due to an impaired Rab5 activation and recruitment of EEA1 towards PI3P-positive organelles.
source: Mechanistically, we find that boutons lacking Piccolo accumulate endocytic vesicles that fail to mature into early endosomes due to an impaired Rab5 activation and recruitment of EEA1 towards PI3P-positive organelles.
evidence: This is a mechanistic summary claim stated in the Discussion section, synthesizing multiple experimental findings.

claim: The observed phenotypes can be restored by the over-expression of Rab5Q79L as well as the Znf1 domain of Piccolo, which interacts with and restores synaptic Pra1 levels, SV pool sizes and SV cycling dynamics in Piccolo deficient synapses.
source: The observed phenotypes can be restored by the over-expression of Rab5Q79L as well as the Znf1 domain of Piccolo, which interacts with and restores synaptic Pra1 levels, SV pool sizes and SV cycling dynamics in Piccolo deficient synapses.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the Discussion section, synthesizing rescue experiment findings.

claim: Piccolo interacts with Prenylated Rab acceptor protein 1 (Pra1).
source: Interestingly, early interaction studies have shown an interaction between Piccolo and the GDI replacement factor (GDF) Pra1 (Fenster et al., 2000), a protein known to promote Rab5 recruitment to endosome membranes where it becomes activated (Abdul-Ghani et al., 2001; Fenster et al., 2000; Hutt et al., 2000; McLauchlan et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature.
